label: Selivanova 2019
setting: vision rehabilitation clinic (Massachusetts Eye and Ear Infirmary, Boston)
diagnosis_mix: macular disease 56.0%; glaucoma 11.9%; optic nerve disease 5.50%; RP/peripheral retinal disease 10.1%; hemianopia 4.59%; other 11.9% (Table 1 n=109)
recruitment: prospective clinical cohort; new patients attending the clinic invited, Dec 2012-Dec 2014; adults, English speaking, no severe hearing or cognitive impairment; 219 declined; 189 completed pre-rehab questionnaires, 109 (58%) completed both
notes: Not a screening/accuracy study: outcome study of pre/post vision rehabilitation change in VRQoL (Rasch logits) and predictors of change (logistic regression, Table 3 p5); no sens/spec or AUC. n_enrolled = 189 who agreed and completed pre questionnaires (p3); n = 109 with pre and post (p3). Age is mean (SD) 68.5 (19.2); median 75 in Discussion p6; age range NR. Mode: mailed for self- or assisted completion, telephone if wished (p2); n_items NR as analysed form differs by subscale (IVI 28 items by item numbering p3; NEI VFQ-25 12-item functioning + 9-item socioemotional scales after Rasch item deletion, driving subscale not used, items A3-A5 added). Visual acuity: best-corrected, better eye, ETDRS logMAR, mean 0.52 (0.41) (Table 1 p4). Admin time NR.
